calls.reason: The packet has no matched January–March compute and revenue series. Friar's post and the Codex-Spark rate-limit note are only context and settle nothing about whether revenue tracked compute.
The BIS papers describe shadow borrowing and links to insurers but rate the risks as moderate. Nothing links media coverage to investor decisions or to deceptive promoters getting rich.
Synergy's estimate of over $25B in 2025 neocloud revenue doesn't separate out hyperscaler purchases. Without customer-level data, the residual Zitron describes can't be measured.

ICONIQ's pre-post survey, reported by Upstarts, shows average AI-product gross margins rising from 41% to 45% in 2025, and application-layer margins rising too. That cuts against the claim that nobody's margins were improving.

The Shen & Tamkin trial found full delegation came at the cost of learning. But participants who asked for explanations kept more, and the authors disclaim causal or long-term conclusions, so the categorical claim is unsettled.
CoreWeave's 10-K puts Microsoft at about 67% in 2025, and the 77% top-two share is from 2024. The demand conclusion is hedged with 'suggests', and the packet has no measure of organic demand.
